predecessors.name: Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth
predecessors.text: parts of Masovia, Podlaskie, the Trakai voivodeship and Žemaitija between East Prussia and the Vistula, Bug and Memel (Neman) rivers

predecessors.name: South Prussia
predecessors.text: the lands of Dobrzyń and Płock northeast of the Vistula

ledger.x: 24 October 1795: the Third Partition gives Prussia New East Prussia.

1795: 'After the Third Partition, the lands of Dobrzyń and Płock northeast of the Vistula river were transferred to New East Prussia'; New East Prussia was divided into the Kammerdepartements of Białystok and Płock.
9 July 1807: 'The area around Białystok was ceded to the Russian Empire, becoming the Belostok Oblast' (Treaties of Tilsit).
9 July 1807: 'The Płock Department and the remainder of the Białystok Department... became part of the Duchy of Warsaw, a French client state'.
9 July 1807: New East Prussia ends ('the Province of New East Prussia was ceded according to the 1807 Treaties of Tilsit'), after Napoleon's victory and the Greater Poland Uprising of 1806.

wars.name: Third Partition of Poland
wars.outcome: After the Kościuszko Uprising (24 March 1794) the powers 'met on 24 October 1795 to dissolve the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth'; Prussia took Podlachia, the rest of Masovia and Warsaw.

certainty.note: Partition treaty lines; the pages give rivers (Vistula, Bug, Memel) as the province's limits but no survey.
